19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
75	- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
76	- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
77	- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开
78	
79	### 2.3 审稿人视角检验
80	
81	写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
82	- 问题是否重要？
83	- 方法是否清楚？
84	- 贡献是否可信？
85	- 结果是否有说服力？
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 三、Introduction 写作规范
90	
91	### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）
92	
93	Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：
94	
95	1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
96	2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
97	3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
98	4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
99	5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献
100	
101	### 3.2 整体叙事结构
102	
103	```
104	现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
105	```
106	
107	### 3.3 禁忌
108	
109	- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
110	- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
111	- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
112	- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
113	- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 四、Related Work 写作规范
118	
119	### 4.1 目标
120	
121	让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。
122	
123	### 4.2 结构要求
124	
125	- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
126	- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
127	- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口
128	
129	### 4.3 禁忌
130	
131	- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
132	- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
133	- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work
134	
135	### 4.4 引用充足度
136	
137	- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
138	- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
139	- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）
144	
145	以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**
146	
147	### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）
148	
149	**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**
150	
151	- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
152	- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
153	- 强制检查命令：
154	  ```bash
155	  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
156	  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
157	  ```
158	- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）
159	
160	### 5.2 段落与句式
161	
162	- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
163	- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
164	- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
165	- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
166	- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容
167	
168	### 5.3 用词黑名单
169	
170	- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
171	- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
172	- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
173	- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用
174	
175	### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）
176	
177	1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
178	2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
179	3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
180	4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 六、图表与视觉规范
185	
186	### 6.1 知识密度原则
187	
188	- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
189	- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
190	- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure
191	
192	### 6.2 表格规范
193	
194	- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
195	- 小数精度全表统一
196	- 最优加粗、次优下划线
197	- Caption 必须自包含
198	
199	### 6.3 图片规范
200	
201	- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
202	- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
203	- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
204	- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页
205	
206	### 6.4 空间效率
207	
208	- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
209	- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
210	- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
211	- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比
212	
213	### 6.5 页面节奏
214	
215	好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：
216	
217	- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
218	- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
219	- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
220	- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
221	- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）
222	
223	### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范
224	
225	**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
226	- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
227	- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
228	- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
229	- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
230	- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）
231	
232	**宽度决策树**：
233	- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
234	- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
235	- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix
236	
237	---
238	
239	## 七、投稿前通用准备
240	
241	### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）
242	
243	- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
244	- **不要用**：
245	  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
246	  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
247	  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
248	- 风险：
249	  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
250	  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
251	  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
252	- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
253	- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致
254	
255	### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对
256	
257	- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
258	- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
259	- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
260	- 行号开启（review 版常需）
261	- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件
262	
263	### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程
264	
265	提交前必须逐一检查：
266	1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
267	2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
268	3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
269	4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
270	5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
271	6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
272	7. 所有专有名词有定义
273	8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
274	9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
275	10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础

- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

## 三、Introduction 写作规范

### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）

Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：

1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

### 3.2 整体叙事结构

```
现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
```

### 3.3 禁忌

- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念

---

## 四、Related Work 写作规范

### 4.1 目标

让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。

### 4.2 结构要求

- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口

### 4.3 禁忌

- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work

### 4.4 引用充足度

- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足

---

## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）

以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**

### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）

**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**

- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
- 强制检查命令：
  ```bash
  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
  ```
- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）

### 5.2 段落与句式

- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容

### 5.3 用词黑名单

- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用

### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）

1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写

---

## 六、图表与视觉规范

### 6.1 知识密度原则

- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure

### 6.2 表格规范

- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
- 小数精度全表统一
- 最优加粗、次优下划线
- Caption 必须自包含

### 6.3 图片规范

- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页

### 6.4 空间效率

- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比

### 6.5 页面节奏

好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：

- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）

### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范

**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）

**宽度决策树**：
- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix

---

## 七、投稿前通用准备

### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）

- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
- **不要用**：
  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
- 风险：
  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致

### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对

- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
- 行号开启（review 版常需）
- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件

### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程

提交前必须逐一检查：
1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
7. 所有专有名词有定义
8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础

33	\subsection{Pixel-Shuffle: Catastrophic Cliff-Edge}
34	\label{sec:smolvla_results}
35	
36	The SmolVLA baseline (bypass mode, all 128 vision tokens) achieves 44.8\% SR (224/500, CI [40.5\%, 49.2\%]).\footnote{The official SmolVLA result is 87.3\% SR with batch size 64 on 8 GPUs. Our reproduction uses a smaller batch due to compute constraints.} Every pruning configuration produces 0\% SR across seven configurations varying scoring (learned ACIS vs.\ random), retention ratio ($k \in \{0.50, 0.70, 0.90, 0.95\}$), and mechanism (zero-masking, true removal, token merging). The official SmolVLA checkpoint (59.2\% SR) exhibits identical failure; the cliff-edge is architectural, not a training artifact.
37	
38	The pattern generalizes across LIBERO suites: Spatial 0.6\%, Goal 0\%. Pixel-shuffle folds each $4{\times}4$ patch block into a single token by channel concatenation; removing one token eliminates an entire $4{\times}4$ receptive field. The resulting spatial entanglement means even 5\% removal ($k{=}0.95$, losing 6 of 128 tokens) destroys task-critical visual information. Full ablation results appear in Table~\ref{tab:smolvla_ablation}, Appendix~\ref{app:smolvla_ablation}.

40	\subsection{MLP Projector: Smooth Graded Degradation}
41	\label{sec:openvla_results}
42	
43	Under random token removal, OpenVLA degrades gracefully across all retention ratios: 74.0\% (baseline) $\rightarrow$ 69.4\% at $k{=}0.95$ ($-4.6$\,pp) $\rightarrow$ 62.0\% at $k{=}0.90$ $\rightarrow$ 49.0\% at $k{=}0.70$ $\rightarrow$ 37.4\% at $k{=}0.50$ $\rightarrow$ 20.6\% at $k{=}0.30$ (Figure~\ref{fig:degradation_curve}; full results with CIs in Table~\ref{tab:openvla_full}, Appendix).\footnote{A second random seed confirms the graded pattern: 62.2\% at $k{=}0.9$ ($+$0.2\,pp), 52.6\% at $k{=}0.7$ ($+$3.6\,pp), 35.6\% at $k{=}0.5$ ($-$1.8\,pp). All within 4\,pp of the primary seed. Per-seed details in Table~\ref{tab:openvla_multiseed}, Appendix~\ref{app:openvla_multiseed}.} At $k{=}0.30$, two tasks reach 0\% SR, but eight retain non-zero performance: degradation is graded, not cliff-edge. Random token removal provides a conservative lower bound on architectural resilience; learned scoring methods would likely yield better retention.
44	
45	OFT~\cite{kim2025openoft} retains OpenVLA's MLP connector but replaces the action head; its attention entropy (0.667) matches standard OpenVLA (0.661). The connector, not the action head, determines token importance structure. EfficientVLA~\cite{yang2025efficientvla} corroborates the graded pattern from the literature: CogACT~\cite{li2024cogact} (MLP projector) retains 74.2\% SR under 78\% pruning.
46	
47	To control for scoring method in cross-architecture comparisons, we evaluate L2 norm-based selection on OpenVLA. At moderate-to-aggressive retention ($k \leq 0.7$), L2 performs within 2--4\,pp of random removal (Table~\ref{tab:openvla_l2_vs_random}, Appendix~\ref{app:l2_vs_random}). At $k{=}0.9$, L2 outperforms random by 8.5\,pp (70.6\% vs.\ 62.0\%, reproducible across two random seeds), consistent with the weak but non-zero importance gradient predicted by CV$\,{=}\,$0.215: the signal is exploitable only when few tokens are removed.

49	\subsection{Linear Projection: From Uniformly Critical to Threshold-Graded}
50	\label{sec:linear_results}
51	
52	Three models share a linear projection connector yet exhibit qualitatively different pruning responses. The divergence traces to what happens \emph{after} the projection: nothing ($\pi_0$), a learned scaling ($\pi_0.5$), or a full 12-layer encoder (X-VLA).
53	
54	\paragraph{$\pi_0$ (3.3B, 256 tokens, pure linear).} Offline normalized L1 action loss at $k{=}0.1$ is 0.976, a 2.4\% \emph{improvement} over the unpruned baseline.\footnote{Offline action loss measures single-step prediction quality; closed-loop evaluation may reveal additional degradation.} CV$\,{=}\,$0.038 indicates near-uniform token norms. Because all tokens carry equal weight, removing 90\% at random preserves spatial coverage and the model compensates.
55	
56	\paragraph{$\pi_0.5$ (4B, 768 tokens, linear $\times\!\sqrt{d}$).} The baseline achieves 98.2\% SR. This model reveals that low CV does not imply pruning immunity; it implies uniform criticality. The response is strongly method-dependent: random removal at $k{=}0.5$ retains 69.4\% SR ($-$28.8\,pp), while L2 norm-based removal at the same ratio collapses to 33.4\% ($-$64.8\,pp). The gap of 36\,pp is the largest method-dependent effect in our study.
57	
58	Random removal produces monotonic degradation: 77.2\% at $k{=}0.7$, 69.4\% at $k{=}0.5$, 36.4\% at $k{=}0.3$. L2 norm selection instead produces a V-shaped curve: 55.0\% at $k{=}0.7$, 33.4\% at $k{=}0.5$ (the valley), 51.0\% at $k{=}0.3$. The non-monotonic L2 pattern arises because norm ranking in a low-CV distribution selects spatially clustered tokens (slight norm variations correlate with image regions), and the resulting loss of spatial coverage peaks at intermediate budgets. A second random seed (seed43) confirms the random result: 68.4\% at $k{=}0.5$ ($\Delta{=}$1.0\,pp from seed42).
59	
60	This result falsifies the ``immune'' assumption from the $\pi_0$ offline evaluation. Low-CV tokens are uniformly critical, not uniformly dispensable. L2 norm-based selection systematically concentrates on spatially correlated tokens and loses coverage; random selection preserves the uniform spatial distribution that these architectures require.
61	
62	\paragraph{X-VLA (880M, 50 tokens, linear + 12-layer BART).} The 99.2\% baseline is maintained at $k{=}0.95$ ($99.1 \pm 0.2$\%, 3 seeds) and $k{=}0.9$ ($97.8 \pm 0.4$\%) under L2 norm-based removal. A sharp cliff appears at $k{=}0.85$ (67.8\%, $-$30\,pp, 2 seeds), with non-monotonic recovery at $k{=}0.80$ (88.6\%) before degradation resumes: $57.2 \pm 1.6$\% at $k{=}0.7$, $43.4 \pm 0.8$\% at $k{=}0.5$, $22.3 \pm 1.1$\% at $k{=}0.3$, $4.7 \pm 0.6$\% at $k{=}0.2$, and near-zero at $k{=}0.1$. The $\pi_0$--OpenVLA controlled comparison (same 256 SigLIP tokens, same encoder lineage, differing only in connector) produces a 63\,pp gap at $k{=}0.1$, isolating the connector pipeline as the causal factor.

lines: \section{Analysis and Discussion}
\label{sec:analysis}
-\subsection{Effective Pipeline Complexity Determines Token Independence}
+\subsection{Connector Determines Token Independence}
\label{sec:pixel_shuffle}

-The $\pi_0$--OpenVLA controlled comparison (Section~\ref{sec:taxonomy_overview}) isolates the connector as causal: 63\,pp gap at $k{=}0.1$ with token count and encoder held constant. The mechanism lies in how each connector creates different token independence structures.

+The seven-model taxonomy (Table~\ref{tab:taxonomy}) spans a continuous spectrum of token independence structures, each dictated by the vision-to-LLM connector rather than model scale or action head design.

-Pixel-shuffle connectors (SmolVLA) apply $4 \times 4$ spatial folding: each of 128 tokens encodes 16 patches via channel concatenation (Figure~\ref{fig:pixel_shuffle}, Appendix~\ref{app:supplementary_figures}). Removing any token eliminates an entire receptive field; the folding is fixed, so no downstream layer can recover discarded information. Pure linear projections ($\pi_0$) map each patch independently with no cross-token interaction, making tokens genuinely interchangeable. X-VLA's 12-layer BART encoder~\cite{lewis2020bart} introduces cross-token mixing that creates partial dependencies (CV $= 0.151$, four times $\pi_0$'s 0.038; entropy $= 0.614$), explaining its threshold-graded pattern; the cliff onset at $k{=}0.85$ ($-30$\,pp) is reproducible across 2 seeds, confirming the threshold is architectural. The narrow cross-seed variance (std $\leq 1.6$\,pp across all retention ratios, 3 seeds $\times$ 500 episodes) confirms that pruning sensitivity is an intrinsic property of the vision-to-LLM pipeline architecture, not an artifact of stochastic evaluation or task initialization. Within the cliff region, a non-monotonic dip at $k{=}0.85$ relative to $k{=}0.80$ (67.8\% vs.\ 88.6\%) reveals that the \emph{identity} of retained tokens matters more than their count: two additional low-importance tokens (L2 rank 41--42 of 50) cause catastrophic interference on 4 of 10 tasks ($\sim$$-50$\,pp each), while the remaining tasks are unaffected. This task-specific sensitivity is consistent with the BART encoder's 12-layer cross-attention creating entangled dependencies that amplify noise from marginal tokens near the critical density. MLP projectors (OpenVLA, OFT) preserve per-patch locality but create partial dependencies through non-linear transformations; Both entropy and CV independently confirm that the connector, not the action head, determines token importance structure: OFT's entropy (0.667) matches OpenVLA's (0.661), and OFT's CV (0.219) matches OpenVLA's (0.215).

+Pixel-shuffle connectors create maximal entanglement. SmolVLA's $4 \times 4$ spatial folding packs 16 patches into each token by channel concatenation (CV $= 0.314$, the highest in our study). The folding is fixed and irreversible: removing one token eliminates an entire receptive field, and no downstream layer can recover the discarded content. Tokens encode non-overlapping spatial regions with heterogeneous visual content, making every token simultaneously essential and non-redundant.

-The non-monotonic relationship between model scale and pruning tolerance provides further evidence that effective pipeline complexity, not parameter count, is the causal factor. Ordered by parameters: SmolVLA (450M) $<$ X-VLA (880M) $<$ $\pi_0$ (3.3B) $<$ OpenVLA (7B). Ordered by pruning tolerance: SmolVLA $<$ OpenVLA $<$ X-VLA $<$ $\pi_0$. The two orderings share only the minimum (SmolVLA); $\pi_0$ at 3.3B is immune while OpenVLA at 7B degrades from $k{=}0.95$, and the CV spectrum (0.038 $\to$ 0.314) tracks connector complexity rather than scale across a 16$\times$ parameter range.

+Pure linear projections produce the opposite extreme. $\pi_0$ maps each SigLIP patch through a single linear layer with no cross-token interaction, yielding CV $= 0.038$ and near-maximal entropy (0.959). Tokens are genuinely interchangeable: any subset preserves the same per-patch information density as any other subset of equal size.
-\subsection{Token Importance Heterogeneity as Predictor}

+$\pi_0.5$ reveals a subtlety that $\pi_0$'s offline-only evaluation conceals. The $\times\!\sqrt{d}$ learned scaling preserves near-uniform norms (CV $= 0.055$), yet the closed-loop response is strongly method-dependent: random removal at $k{=}0.5$ retains 69.4\% SR while L2 norm-based removal collapses to 33.4\%. The 36\,pp gap arises because L2 ranking in a low-CV distribution selects spatially clustered tokens whose slight norm variations correlate with image regions, destroying the spatial coverage that this architecture requires. Random selection preserves uniform spatial distribution by construction. The correct characterization is ``uniformly critical'': every token carries equal weight, making the population robust to uniform subsampling but fragile to any selection method that introduces spatial bias.

+X-VLA's 12-layer BART encoder~\cite{lewis2020bart} introduces cross-token mixing through self-attention, creating partial dependencies that place it between the linear and MLP extremes (CV $= 0.151$, entropy $= 0.614$, the lowest among models). The resulting behavior is threshold-graded: performance holds through $k{=}0.9$ before a sharp cliff at $k{=}0.85$ ($-$30\,pp). The cliff onset is reproducible across seeds (std $\leq$ 1.6\,pp), confirming it as an architectural property.

+MLP projectors (OpenVLA, OFT) apply per-patch non-linear transformations that create partial importance differentiation without cross-token entanglement. OpenVLA's CV (0.215) and OFT's CV (0.219) match within measurement noise, as do their entropy values (0.661 vs.\ 0.667); the connector, not the action head, determines token importance structure. CogACT~\cite{li2024cogact} corroborates the graded pattern from the literature (74.2\% SR under 78\% pruning). The smooth degradation profile reflects a moderate importance gradient that scoring methods can partially exploit at high retention but that offers diminishing returns under aggressive compression.

+Parameter count does not predict pruning tolerance. Ordered by scale: SmolVLA (450M) $<$ X-VLA (880M) $<$ $\pi_0$ (3.3B) $<$ $\pi_0.5$ (4B) $<$ OpenVLA (7B). Ordered by tolerance, SmolVLA remains the minimum, but $\pi_0$ and $\pi_0.5$ at 3.3--4B surpass OpenVLA at 7B, and X-VLA at 880M tolerates more aggressive pruning than OpenVLA. The CV spectrum (0.038 to 0.314) tracks connector complexity rather than parameter count across a 16$\times$ scale range.
+\subsection{CV as Dual Predictor}
\label{sec:diagnostic}

-The coefficient of variation (CV) of token importance L2 norms forms a continuous spectrum that predicts both the class and onset of degradation: $\pi_0$ (0.038) is immune through $k{=}0.1$, X-VLA (0.151) cliffs at $k{=}0.85$, OpenVLA (0.215) and OFT (0.219) degrade from $k{=}0.95$, SmolVLA (0.314) collapses at $k{=}0.95$.

+Token importance CV predicts both the tolerance class of a model and the optimal pruning strategy, a dual prediction that emerges from a single mechanistic principle: CV measures the strength of the importance gradient that scoring methods can exploit.

-Attention entropy explains why. $\pi_0$'s entropy is 0.959 (near-uniform, range 0.931--0.983): low CV + high entropy means tokens are interchangeable, so any subset is equivalent to uniform downsampling. SmolVLA presents an apparent paradox: high entropy (0.952) yet catastrophic pruning. The resolution is that tokens are uniformly \emph{attended} but carry heterogeneous \emph{content} due to pixel-shuffle folding---``differentiated but entangled.'' X-VLA's entropy (0.614, lowest among models) reflects partial differentiation from the BART encoder, predicting the \emph{onset point} of degradation rather than merely a categorical class. OpenVLA shows progressive sharpening from 0.98 to 0.48 across layers (Figure~\ref{fig:entropy_layers}, Appendix~\ref{app:supplementary_figures}), consistent with its graded regime. CV requires only a single forward pass on task-relevant frames, providing a zero-cost, single-forward-pass predictor of pruning tolerance. CV also predicts scoring method utility: OpenVLA's moderate CV (0.215) implies a weak importance gradient, and L2 norm-based selection outperforms random by only 0.8--4.4\,pp at $k \leq 0.7$ but by 8.5\,pp at $k{=}0.9$ where few tokens are removed and the gradient is most exploitable (Section~\ref{sec:openvla_results}).

+Low-CV models have near-uniform L2 norms. L2 norm ranking in this regime captures spatial artifacts (slight norm variations that correlate with image position) rather than genuine importance differences. Selection based on these artifacts concentrates retained tokens on spatially correlated patches, destroying the uniform coverage that low-CV architectures depend on. Random selection preserves spatial uniformity by construction. The mechanism predicts that the random-over-L2 advantage should grow as CV decreases, and the data in Table~\ref{tab:scaling_law} confirm this at two retention ratios. At $k{=}0.5$: $\Delta = +$36.0\,pp ($\pi_0.5$, CV $= 0.055$) $\to$ $+$26.9\,pp (X-VLA, CV $= 0.151$) $\to$ $-$3.4\,pp (OpenVLA, CV $= 0.215$). At $k{=}0.7$: the same monotonic ordering holds ($+$22.2\,pp $\to$ $+$7.0\,pp $\to$ pending). The pattern persists across a 2$\times$ change in absolute token budget, strengthening the interpretation from a coincidence at a single operating point to a structural property of the connector.
-\subsection{Why Re-Encoding Succeeds Where Deletion Fails}

+High-CV models present a genuine importance gradient where L2 norm ranking aligns with actual information content. OpenVLA (CV $= 0.215$) sits near the crossover: L2 outperforms random by 8.5\,pp at $k{=}0.9$ where the gradient is most exploitable, but the advantage shrinks to 2--4\,pp at $k \leq 0.7$ as the proportion of removed tokens exceeds the gradient's discriminative range.

+Extreme compression introduces a partial reversal. At $k{=}0.3$, $\pi_0.5$'s L2 selection achieves 51.0\% SR vs.\ random's 36.4\%. When very few tokens remain, even spatially clustered high-norm tokens provide more signal than a sparse random sample. The reversal does not invalidate the CV predictor; it adds a budget-dependent interaction that future work should characterize across more models.

+Attention entropy provides a mechanistic supplement that resolves an apparent paradox. SmolVLA's entropy (0.952) is nearly as high as $\pi_0$'s (0.959), yet SmolVLA collapses under any pruning. SmolVLA's tokens are uniformly \emph{attended} but carry heterogeneous \emph{content} due to pixel-shuffle folding. Entropy captures how the LLM allocates attention across tokens; CV captures the input-side importance structure. Entropy alone cannot distinguish ``interchangeable'' ($\pi_0$) from ``entangled'' (SmolVLA), but CV separates them cleanly (0.038 vs.\ 0.314). OpenVLA's progressive entropy sharpening from 0.98 to 0.48 across layers (Figure~\ref{fig:entropy_layers}, Appendix~\ref{app:supplementary_figures}) is consistent with a graded regime where the LLM progressively concentrates on higher-importance tokens.

+CV therefore serves as a zero-cost, single-forward-pass diagnostic with practical implications: models below CV $\approx 0.15$ should use coverage-preserving methods (random or spatially uniform selection), while models above this threshold can benefit from importance-based scoring. The current validation spans three models and two retention ratios; formal use as a quantitative predictor requires additional architectures and operating points.
+\subsection{Why Re-Encoding Succeeds}
\label{sec:learned_compression}

-Two architecturally distinct modules---cross-attention pooling (22.2M) and a parameter-matched MLP adapter (22.14M)---both recover $\sim$60--63\% SR on SmolVLA where deletion yields 0\% ($p = 0.15$), identifying learned re-encoding as the operative factor. The flat M-curve ($M{=}16$: 56.9\% through $M{=}128$: 58.0\%) shows VTR redistributes information without destroying it, even at $8\times$ compression. The $M{=}128$ passthrough gains 13pp over baseline (44.8\% $\to$ 58.0\%), confirming re-encoding adds value through feature reorganization independent of compression.

+Learned re-encoding overcomes pixel-shuffle failure because it breaks the rigid spatial entanglement that the $4 \times 4$ folding creates. Cross-attention pooling integrates information across receptive field boundaries, redistributing content from the original 128 tokens into $M$ compressed representations no longer tied to fixed spatial blocks.

-The mechanism is specific to pixel-shuffle pathology: re-encoding breaks the rigid $4 \times 4$ spatial entanglement by integrating information across receptive field boundaries. On OpenVLA (MLP projector), VTR yields 0\% SR even in passthrough mode, indicating disruption rather than useful reorganization (Section~\ref{sec:smart_compress_results}). VTR succeeds precisely where deletion fails---architectures whose rigid entanglement demands learned redistribution.

+The $M{=}128$ passthrough configuration confirms that re-encoding, not compression, is the operative mechanism. Passthrough adds parameters without reducing token count, yet gains 13\,pp over the baseline (44.8\% $\to$ 58.0\%). The flat M-curve ($M{=}16$: 56.9\% through $M{=}128$: 58.0\%, all five values within 5\,pp) shows that once entanglement is broken, token count is secondary.
-\subsection{Offline Metrics Underestimate Closed-Loop Degradation}

+A parameter-matched MLP adapter (22.14M parameters) achieves 63.4\% SR at $M{=}32$, statistically indistinguishable from cross-attention ($p = 0.15$). Re-encoding through any learned mapping that integrates across token boundaries suffices; the attention mechanism itself is not essential.

+The remedy is specific to the pathology. VTR applied to OpenVLA yields 0\% SR even in passthrough mode, confirming that re-encoding disrupts rather than assists architectures whose tokens already carry independent per-patch information. VTR succeeds precisely on architectures whose rigid entanglement demands learned redistribution.
+\subsection{Offline Metrics Underestimate Closed-Loop}
\label{sec:metric_disconnect}

-Offline metrics underestimate pruning-induced failure. The $3.4\times$ action error increase (Appendix~\ref{app:offline_error}) is a negative signal, but per-step averages dilute catastrophic events (gripper inversion, L2 $= 1.02$) that individually terminate episodes. X-VLA exemplifies this disconnect: offline loss at $k{=}0.3$ is 1.0014 (near-baseline), yet closed-loop SR is $22.3 \pm 1.1$\% ($-77$pp). Offline evaluation provides directional signals but closed-loop evaluation is essential for validating VLA compression.
+Offline evaluation systematically underestimates pruning-induced failure because per-step averages dilute catastrophic single-step events that individually terminate episodes.

+X-VLA at $k{=}0.3$ demonstrates the gap directly: offline loss is 1.0014 (near-baseline), yet closed-loop SR drops to 22.3\% ($-$77\,pp). A single gripper inversion (L2 $= 1.02$) is a minor perturbation in average action error but terminates an episode irreversibly. $\pi_0$'s offline loss at $k{=}0.1$ shows a 2.4\% \emph{improvement} over the unpruned baseline, a result that closed-loop evaluation may contradict if similar catastrophic events occur at deployment frequency.

+$\pi_0.5$ adds a distinct form of evidence: the 36\,pp gap between L2 and random removal at $k{=}0.5$ is invisible to any offline metric that averages across token subsets or selection methods. Offline evaluation would report degradation for both methods; only closed-loop evaluation reveals that the \emph{choice} of pruning strategy, not just the pruning ratio, determines whether the model remains functional.
\subsection{Limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}

-All closed-loop experiments use the LIBERO simulation benchmark, which does not capture real-world deployment conditions such as sensor noise, calibration drift, and physical contact dynamics. Scale confounding is partially addressed: the pruning tolerance ordering (SmolVLA $<$ OpenVLA $<$ X-VLA $<$ $\pi_0$) is non-monotonic with parameter count (450M $<$ 880M $<$ 3.3B $<$ 7B), sharing only the minimum, and the CV spectrum tracks connector complexity continuously across a 16$\times$ parameter range (Section~\ref{sec:pixel_shuffle}). A matched-scale experiment (same LLM backbone, different connectors) remains the ideal control but is not currently feasible: no public VLA model pair shares an identical backbone while differing only in connector design. The $\pi_0$--OpenVLA controlled comparison (same encoder lineage, same token count, different connector) provides the closest available approximation.
+All closed-loop experiments use the LIBERO simulation benchmark, which does not capture real-world conditions such as sensor noise, calibration drift, and physical contact dynamics.

-$\pi_0$ evaluation is currently offline only; closed-loop results may reveal additional degradation not captured by single-step loss, as demonstrated by X-VLA's offline-to-closed-loop gap (Section~\ref{sec:metric_disconnect}). X-VLA results at $k{=}0.1$ are based on a single seed; multi-seed confirmation is pending.

+The seven models span three connector families but differ in LLM backbone (PaliGemma for $\pi_0$/$\pi_0.5$, Llama-2 for OpenVLA, Qwen2 for SmolVLA), preventing clean isolation of the connector effect from backbone differences. The $\pi_0$--OpenVLA controlled comparison (same 256 SigLIP tokens, same encoder lineage) provides the closest available approximation, but a matched-backbone experiment remains the ideal control.

-VTR succeeds on SmolVLA's pixel-shuffle connector but yields 0\% SR on OpenVLA's MLP projector, indicating that re-encoding is specific to the spatial entanglement pathology rather than a general compression technique. Re-encoding on the well-trained official SmolVLA checkpoint yields 53.4\% SR, below the 59.2\% uncompressed baseline. The gain on our fine-tuned model (44.8\% $\to$ 60.1\%) is larger, consistent with re-encoding providing the most benefit when baseline features are undertrained.

+The spatial clustering hypothesis for L2 failure on low-CV models lacks direct visualization evidence. Token position analysis that maps selected tokens back to image coordinates would confirm whether L2 ranking concentrates on spatially correlated patches; this analysis is pending.

+Data collection is approximately 85\% complete. OpenVLA L2 results at $k{=}0.7$ are pending, and $\pi_0.5$ additional seed runs are in progress. $\pi_0$ evaluation remains offline only; closed-loop results may reveal degradation not captured by single-step loss.

+The CV scaling law is validated at three models and two retention ratios. Extending the validation to additional architectures and benchmarks is necessary before CV can serve as a formal quantitative predictor rather than a qualitative diagnostic.
